newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banacci Q3 net seen obscuring weaknesses.
newsitem.headline: Banacci Q3 net seen obscuring weaknesses.

text.p: Falling interest margins for Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival S.A. (Banacci) cast a shadow on what was otherwise a healthy third-quarter net profit, analysts said on Tuesday.
Banacci's third-quarter net profit rose to 1.422 billion pesos from 1.177 billion pesos in the same period last year.
Banamex, the group's bank unit, reported a third-quarter net income of 601 million pesos, up 13 percent compared with profit in the third quarter of 1995.

"The reduction (in margins) is explained by the higher share of government securities ... in the bank's total earning assets, as well as the higher share of UDI-denominated loans," Banacci said in a statement.
The third quarter's rise in real interest rates -- and their effect on margins -- could prove to be a problem for Mexican banks in the fourth quarter if recent peso weakness continued, analysts said.
Most analysts said they would reduce their year-end earnings estimates on Banacci but still liked the bank's medium-term prospects.
Sanchez said he was interested in seeing if Banamex could pass on its higher borrowing costs to depositors without losing market share in an increasingly competitive banking environment.

Analysts had mixed feelings on Banamex's move to create 1.66 billion pesos in reserve provisions during the quarter. The move took provisions to 84 percent of gross past-due loans versus 75 percent at the end of June.
Some analysts said the move fell short of the aggressive reserve creation by the bank's rivals, Grupo Financiero Serfin and Grupo Financiero Bancomer.

Rogelio Urrutia, a bank analyst at Valores Finamex in Mexico City, said Banamex would have to create an additional three billion pesos in reserves to meet U.S. GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) standards to be implemented next year.
Mexican banks by law have to conform to GAAP by the first quarter of next year. That will generally mean a big rise in loans considered past due.

Still, Banamex's asset quality appears to be slowly improving. During the third quarter, past-due loans grew four percent, down from five percent during the second quarter and nine percent during the first three months of the year.
